blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — epinephrine auto-injector storage and inspection
stem: A client carries an epinephrine auto-injector for anaphylaxis. Which statement shows correct understanding of storage and maintenance?

options.A: I will keep it at room temperature, protect it from light, inspect the solution periodically, and replace it before expiration or if the solution becomes cloudy, discolored, or contains particles.
options.B: I will refrigerate it to preserve potency, keep it in the refrigerator door for quick access, and use it until the expiration date even if the solution becomes slightly cloudy.
options.C: I will store it in my vehicle so it is always nearby, because brief exposure to summer heat or winter cold does not affect an epinephrine auto-injector.
options.D: I will keep it protected from light, but I do not need to inspect the solution or replace it before expiration as long as the device has never been used.

rationale: Current epinephrine auto-injector labeling instructs storage at controlled room temperature, protection from light, avoidance of refrigeration and extreme heat or cold, periodic inspection through the viewing window, replacement if the solution becomes discolored, cloudy, or contains particles, and replacement before the expiration date. Therefore A is the best answer. B incorrectly recommends refrigeration and continued use of cloudy solution, C exposes the device to temperature extremes, and D omits required visual inspection and expiration replacement.
educational_objective: Teach epinephrine auto-injector maintenance: store at room temperature protected from light, avoid extreme heat/cold and refrigeration, inspect solution periodically, and replace for abnormal appearance or before expiration.
source_document_title: Epinephrine Injection, USP Auto-Injector — Prescribing Information and Patient Information
source_version_date: Prescribing information revised August 2018; current DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §16.2 Storage and Handling: protect from light; store at 20–25°C, excursions 15–30°C; do not refrigerate; replace if solution is discolored, cloudy, or contains particles. Patient Information: avoid extreme heat/cold, inspect periodically, replace before expiration.
source_claim_supported: Epinephrine auto-injectors should be stored at room temperature protected from light, not refrigerated or exposed to extremes, visually inspected, and replaced for abnormal solution appearance or before expiration.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: educate clients about medications; maintain medication safety; review storage and administration requirements for emergency medications.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rebuilt all four options as full storage-and-maintenance plans rather than one detailed correct statement against short distractors.
Added current label-supported room-temperature, light-protection, visual-inspection, and expiration criteria to the stem's single best-answer construct.
Made each distractor contain one or more realistic maintenance errors rather than implausible absolutes.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current storage and patient-information instructions. B recommends refrigeration and use of cloudy solution, C accepts temperature extremes, and D omits periodic inspection and timely replacement. No second defensible answer remains; option lengths are sufficiently substantive that length does not function as a reliable cue.
